smell: remoteISO256 builds the remote ssh command via raw string concat ("sha256sum "+target where target = remotePath+"/"+filename), then calls phase.SSHRun which feeds the whole string to ssh's trailing arg — the remote login shell evaluates it. Sibling phase/iso_cleanup.go shellSingleQuote-wraps every atom; this site bypasses that template and accepts whatever metacharacters land in filename (filepath.Base of an ISO path derived from cluster machine names that flow from config).
evidence:
target := remotePath + "/" + filename
result, err := phase.SSHRun(ctx, exec, host, "sha256sum "+target)
severity_reason: Config-controlled value (machine name → ISO filename) flows unescaped into a remote shell evaluation; the canonical sibling pattern (iso_cleanup.go shellSingleQuote) exists to prevent exactly this — rubric §4/known-exploit-path adjacent.
fix_summary: Switch to phase.SSHRunArgv(ctx, exec, host, "sha256sum", "--", target) — argv mode still hands ssh a joined command but each atom is preserved verbatim, and a leading -- guards filenames starting with -. Or, mirror iso_cleanup.go: phase.SSHRun(ctx, exec, host, "sha256sum -- "+shellSingleQuote(target)).
rule_source: internal/distribution/okd/phase/ssh.go:L43-L48 doc: argv mode does NOT bypass the shell
must_preserve: phase.SSHRun and phase.SSHRunArgv are canonical wrappers — don't introduce a third ssh helper; use the existing argv-mode helper.

smell: AddRepo shells out to dpkg --print-architecture to derive the apt sources.list arch=… token. Go stdlib's runtime.GOARCH is the same value for the architectures okdctl ships (amd64, arm64) and is already used in internal/platform/platform.go DownloadArch / CoreOSArch — so this subprocess adds a runtime dep on dpkg and a fork+exec for a constant-at-build value.
fix_summary: Replace with platform.DownloadArch() (or runtime.GOARCH directly): both already resolve amd64/arm64 the same way Debian dpkg does. Removes one fork+exec from every AddRepo and removes a hard dep on dpkg being on PATH.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §dependencies (check whether Go 1.25 stdlib covers it)
repo-counter-example: internal/platform/platform.go:L26-L40 (DownloadArch / CoreOSArch already use runtime.GOARCH)
must_preserve: AddRepo's Debian sources.list-d write semantics; only the arch-detection step changes.

smell: installHashiCorpDebianRepo shells out to lsb_release -cs to read the Debian codename, but /etc/os-release VERSION_CODENAME exposes the same value and is already parsed by internal/platform/platform.go (Detect). lsb_release is a Python script that ships separately on Debian/Ubuntu — relying on it adds a runtime dep and a fork+exec for data already in memory.
fix_summary: Add a VERSION_CODENAME field to platform.Detect()'s output (it already parses /etc/os-release) or expose a small parseOSReleaseField(VERSION_CODENAME) helper, then call it here. Removes the lsb_release dep — older Debian/RHEL installations don't ship it by default.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §dependencies (check whether Go 1.25 stdlib covers it)
must_preserve: HashiCorp GPG fingerprint pinning at expectedHashiCorpGPGFingerprint and the WriteTempFile + CopyFile install pattern stay untouched.

smell: DetectBackend probes ufw with a raw exec.CommandContext + cmd.Output() and a manual *exec.ExitError unwrap, while every other shellout in the same file (Configure, modifyPort, etc.) goes through system.RunCaptured / system.OutputCaptured. The canonical wrappers already filter env through executor.DefaultEnvAllowlist, capture stderr into the returned error, and centralise diagnostics — bypassing them on this one path inherits the parent shell's env (including AWS_*/GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN tokens that the allowlist drops).
fix_summary: Replace with output, err := system.OutputCaptured(ctx, ufw, status); on err, log via the same debug fall-through (system.OutputCaptured already wraps stderr into the returned error). Same env-filter and stderr-into-err semantics as the rest of this file.
rule_source: repo-counter-example: same file uses system.RunCaptured at L134, L188, L215, L221, L233
must_preserve: The probe-style fall-through behaviour (a non-zero exit from ufw must NOT abort DetectBackend; it must drop through to iptables) and the logger.Debug observability for failed probes.

smell: defaultStartMonitorCmd uses exec.CommandContext (defaults to SIGKILL on ctx cancel) AND a hand-rolled kill func that the orchestrator calls on <-ctx.Done(). On install timeout, openshift-install gets SIGKILL'd before it can flush its in-flight diagnostic output (the very thing the operator needs to debug a 60-minute install that just timed out). Go 1.20 cmd.Cancel + cmd.WaitDelay supersede the hand-rolled kill: SIGTERM first, then a bounded wait, then SIGKILL.
fix_summary: Set cmd.Cancel = func() error { return cmd.Process.Signal(syscall.SIGTERM) } and cmd.WaitDelay = 30 * time.Second before cmd.Start(). Drop the hand-rolled kill / sync.OnceFunc — exec already coordinates the cancel-then-wait-then-kill flow. Then the reapTimer in MonitorInstallation also collapses.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §concurrency (every goroutine needs a stop signal or a documented leak bound)
must_preserve: openshift-install must still SIGKILL eventually if it ignores SIGTERM; the buffered doneCh + Wait goroutine semantics; the existing 30s reap window in MonitorInstallation. The streaming to os.Stdout/os.Stderr stays as-is so users see live install output.

smell: ringWriter caps retained completed lines at constMaxLines=200 but the partial buffer (incomplete current line, no trailing newline yet) grows without bound. A subprocess that writes a long blob without a newline (e.g. a single JSON object spanning megabytes, or a binary that streams progress without newlines) would balloon partial — and Result.Stdout/Stderr emit the full partial as the tail's last entry. Affects every Run / RunChecked / RunStreamed site.
fix_summary: Cap r.partial at e.g. 64 KiB: if len(r.partial) > maxPartial, push the truncated chunk as a synthetic line (or drop it and start over). One safe shape: when partial would exceed the cap, r.push(r.partial[:maxPartial]); r.partial = r.partial[maxPartial:]. Subprocesses that misbehave now lose the newline-less tail — an acceptable trade for a hard memory bound.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes (canonical helpers — Executor must stay safe for every caller)
must_preserve: The 200-line tail behaviour for well-behaved newline-terminated subprocesses; the line ordering in tail() output.
